races.title: State House, District 120
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Karl Gillespie
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 120 (Cherokee, Clay, Graham and Macon counties) since 2021. Macon County commissioner 2016–2020. Founder and president of National Communications, Inc., a low-voltage communications contractor started in 1999. Cattle farmer and former vice president of Globe Communications.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Karl Gillespie was born or raised, or when he moved to his current home. We found no documented actions, such as bills he sponsored or official filings, that clearly bear on the platform issues. His campaign site gives only general statements on taxes, education, natural resources and economic development, and none address data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, immigration, policing, guns or abortion. We found no stated positions on data centers or specific development projects, no news reports of controversies and no notable endorsements. Ballotpedia lists none for 2024 or 2026, and he did not complete its candidate surveys. We found no foreign ties.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2021 and was a Macon County commissioner 2016–2020. Founded and runs National Communications, Inc. (since 1999). He lists a House leadership post (Majority Whip) and Appropriations leadership roles on his campaign site.
qual.why: Scored high for more than five years of legislative service, prior local elected office and more than 25 years of business ownership. He has no law or formal policy career in the sources. The committee chair roles and the Majority Whip post, which appears only on his own campaign site, were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Caleb Brown
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for NC House District 120 in 2026. High school social studies teacher and varsity soccer coach in Highlands, NC, and a 2nd Lieutenant in the North Carolina Army National Guard. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed as recommended in the Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy voter guide (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find Caleb Brown's birthplace or exact birth year, only that he is originally from South Carolina and about 33 years old. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or police pay. We also found no records of actions in office, since he has never held office. Information on his military service is limited to Ballotpedia's note that he has served since 2020 and his own description as a 2nd Lieutenant. The campaign site's issue pages say nothing on most topics beyond education, healthcare and household finances.

local.label: Roots 40: He is originally from South Carolina and says he has called Highlands, NC home for the last seven years, which puts his move to North Carolina at under 10 years ago; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Seven years as a high school Social Studies teacher and varsity soccer coach, a school bus driver, and a 2nd Lieutenant in the NC Army National Guard. He has no prior elected or legislative office.
qual.why: He is a first-time candidate with no legislative, law, policy or budget career and no local elected office; his work is in an unrelated occupation (teaching), so he scores in the low band.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says public tax dollars should not fund private school vouchers or private schools, and opposes the HB10 voucher extension; he also says he will fight for greater investment in public schools. He did not state a position on a teacher pay raise.
